purpose: How a plating-bench operator converts a specified gold thickness into a verified deposit: estimating true plateable surface area, setting current density inside the bath TDS window, planning run time by Faraday arithmetic corrected by the shop's measured efficiency, setting up and verifying the rectifier and its meters within manufacturer instructions, engineering current distribution on complex shapes with shields, robbers and auxiliary anodes as classes, and proving delivered microns by XRF or witness coupon at the significant surfaces.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
commercial plating chemistry only, operated per the specific product's technical data sheet (TDS); no DIY bath formulation from raw chemicals
the piece arrives prep-complete (water-break-free, activated) and the bath arrives verified in its TDS window by the bath-chemistry discipline; this KB consumes both as inputs

handbook-class relationships (Faraday arithmetic for monovalent gold at density near 19.3 g/cm3, efficiency classes per bath family) are cited only as handbook-class orientation; the TDS and the shop's own measured runs govern every setpoint
the operator is formally trained on the equipment and the chemical hazards present, and the shop verifies its jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules
exclusions: layer architecture and underplating — strike layers, nickel/palladium/white-bronze barrier classes, copper leveling, diffusion mechanisms, flash-vs-heavy build per wear class, duplex systems and topcoats belong to the layer-architecture KB; this KB only flags that a starved zone exposing a nickel underplate on skin-contact jewelry raises the nickel-release compliance class (verify jurisdiction)

fixturing and run handling — rack vs barrel vs brush decisions, wiring and contact-point placement on the piece, agitation setup and part positioning, drag-out management, inter-tank rinse sequence and the full job log belong to the fixturing KB; this KB owns only the electrical consequences and the electrical page of the record

bath selection, analysis, replenishment and contamination management — the bath-chemistry specialist's territory; this KB treats a healthy in-window bath as an input and routes chemical suspicion back to it

numeric setpoints (current density, temperature, time, efficiency) asserted as universal fact — setpoints belong to the specific commercial product's TDS and the shop's own logged history; this KB teaches mechanisms and verification only

mains-side electrical work, rectifier internals, or any wiring method the equipment manufacturer's instructions do not sanction — such work is serviced by qualified persons per the manufacturer, never improvised at the bench
forcing a piece that cannot be contacted or racked without damage — that piece is escalated to the intake/customer decision, never forced through the tanks

formal QC acceptance testing, adhesion and porosity test protocols, and customer-facing thickness or wear claims — the quality-and-finish specialist's territory; this KB hands over measured thickness evidence, not claims
personalized legal or medical advice — nickel-allergy and exposure topics route to regulation classes and professional care

competency_questions.question: How do I estimate the plateable surface area of an irregular piece well enough to set current, and when is a quick estimate not good enough?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SURFACE_AREA_ESTIMATION names the method classes (geometric decomposition, CAD/scan area, gauge-and-length arithmetic, per-SKU cards), the complexity allowance, and the rule that estimation rigor scales with thickness spec and job risk

competency_questions.question: What does current density actually control in the deposit, and what do too high and too low each do on my bench?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CURRENT_DENSITY_MECHANISM states rate/grain/brightness/color as CD-governed with burn symptoms at high CD and slow/dull outcomes at low CD, and LIMITING_CURRENT_CEILING explains the mass-transport ceiling and what raises it

competency_questions.question: Where does my usable current-density window come from, and what am I allowed to state without the TDS in hand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TDS_AND_LOG_DOCTRINE binds every setpoint to the specific product's TDS plus the shop's logged runs and restricts handbook ranges to orientation only

competency_questions.question: How do I turn a target of so-many microns into amperes and minutes, and how sure can I be of the answer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FARADAY_ESTIMATION derives amperes from CD times area and minutes from ampere-minutes per micron scaled by efficiency, always labeled an estimate pending measurement

competency_questions.question: My measured thickness came in far under the Faraday estimate — why, and what do I do now?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EFFICIENCY_CALIBRATION names efficiency drift (bath family, age, CD, temperature, contamination) as the usual cause and prescribes recalibrating minutes-per-micron from the first-article measurement before extending the run

competency_questions.question: How do I set up the rectifier — mode, sizing, ripple, meters — and know I can trust what its panel tells me, without stepping outside the manufacturer's instructions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECTIFIER_SETUP_CC specifies constant-current mode with amperes sized as CD times total immersed area, METER_VERIFICATION requires reference cross-checks and voltage sanity reading, and EQUIPMENT_SAFETY_BOUNDARY forbids any wiring outside manufacturer instructions

competency_questions.question: Why must current be flowing before the piece enters the tank, and what happens to a load that went in dead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LIVE_ENTRY_DISCIPLINE explains immersion (displacement) deposition as the adhesion-killing mechanism and routes a dead-entry load to the strip/replate decision rather than plating over it

competency_questions.question: How do I predict which parts of a complex piece will plate thick and which will starve before I switch anything on?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CURRENT_DISTRIBUTION_MAP identifies edges/tips/rims as high-CD zones and recesses/bores as low-CD zones shaped by geometry and throwing power, and ANODE_GEOMETRY explains how anode area, spacing and symmetry move that field

competency_questions.question: When do I reach for a shield, a current robber, or an auxiliary anode — and what does each one cost me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SHIELDS_AND_ROBBERS distinguishes the free shield from the gold-consuming robber and AUXILIARY_ANODES covers feeding starved zones with maker-sanctioned wiring only, each with its risk named

competency_questions.question: What do I watch while the run is live, and what tells me to stop before the load is scrap?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IN_RUN_MONITORING lists cell-voltage drift, gas pattern and first darkening at high-CD points as watch signals with an explicit stop rule and logged interruptions

competency_questions.question: How do I verify the delivered thickness — XRF or witness coupon — and where on the piece must the measurement be taken?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIRST_ARTICLE_XRF requires measuring the first article of every batch at significant surfaces, WITNESS_COUPON_METHOD covers coupon position fidelity, and SIGNIFICANT_SURFACE_DELIVERY judges minimum thickness where it matters

competency_questions.question: What must the electrical record of a run contain so the next run starts smarter than this one did?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AMPERE_MINUTE_RECORD lists area and method, set current and CD, time, ampere-minutes, planned vs measured thickness, interruptions and any shield/robber/aux hardware used

competency_questions.question: What do I do when the inside of a ring or a deep recess cannot reach the specified thickness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer offers the auxiliary/conforming anode class, honest disclosure of the spread against the significant-surface definition, and the nickel-release compliance flag when a starved zone over a nickel underplate will touch skin

competency_questions.question: What does 'delivering the specified microns' actually commit the bench to, and where is the line between an estimate and a claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THICKNESS_DELIVERY_FRAME states the delivery contract (target thickness at named significant surfaces, verified by measurement) and the rule that Faraday arithmetic plans a run but never backs a claim

glossary.definition: Amperes of plating current per unit of immersed cathode area (A/dm2 class of units); the master variable of electrodeposition — it sets deposition rate, grain, brightness and burn risk, and its usable window comes from the bath's TDS.

The mass-transport ceiling above which gold complex cannot reach the cathode film fast enough and the deposit turns powdery or burnt; it rises with agitation, temperature and metal concentration and falls as a bath depletes.

The unit of delivered charge the bench actually books: current multiplied by time; by Faraday's law the deposited mass — and so the thickness over a known area — is proportional to ampere-minutes times cathode efficiency.

The fraction of delivered charge that deposits gold rather than evolving gas or driving side reactions; a property of the specific bath in its current state, differing by bath family and drifting with age, current density and contamination.
A bath-class property describing how evenly a chemistry distributes deposit between high and low current-density zones; poor throw exaggerates thick edges and starved recesses on complex shapes.

Entering the work into the tank with current already flowing, so electrodeposition starts instantly and no chemical displacement (immersion) film can form; the unconditional entry discipline for gold over less-noble surfaces.
Gold that plates itself chemically onto a less-noble metal without current — a smutty, non-adherent film that dooms adhesion of everything plated on top; the failure a live entry exists to prevent.

A sacrificial cathodic surface wired near a high current-density zone to draw off excess current; it flattens distribution but plates gold onto itself, a real gold cost that must enter amp sizing and job cost.
An extra insoluble anode — platinized-titanium or MMO class — placed into or near a recess to carry the field into a starved zone; wired only by methods the equipment manufacturer sanctions.

A small piece of known substrate and measured area plated with the load at a deliberate position, whose measured thickness verifies delivery where the geometry defeats direct XRF; its position is part of the method.

nodes.definition: Fix what electrical control owns before any knob turns: the job arrives with a target thickness on named significant surfaces (set upstream by the spec and wear class), a chosen bath system, and a designed layer stack — this discipline converts that target into area, current, time and a measured result. The frame draws the honest line the whole KB stands on: delivered thickness is a measured quantity; the Faraday plan is a planning estimate, and no number reaches the QC gate or the customer that did not come from XRF or a witness coupon. It also names the outputs owed downstream: verified microns at the significant surfaces and a complete electrical record of how they were delivered.

included: outputs owed to QC and the record
excluded: setting the thickness spec or wear class
layer stack design
pricing the job

pros.claim: A stated estimate-versus-claim line stops arithmetic from ever being sold as delivered microns
pros.example: a quoted 2.5-micron heavy-wear job releases on the XRF reading at the ring's wear band, never on the minutes it soaked

cons.claim: Insisting on measurement for every delivery statement adds cost and turnaround on trivially small flash jobs
cons.example: a batch of decorative flash pendants where per-piece XRF would cost more than the gold applied

failure_modes: treating the Faraday time plan as proof of thickness and releasing unmeasured work
accepting a job with no named significant surfaces so nobody can say where the microns must land
acceptance_tests: every accepted run states target thickness, the named significant surfaces, the bath system and stack it rides on, and the measurement method that will certify delivery
revisit_triggers: the intake spec format or the significant-surface convention changes
a released job is challenged on thickness and the record cannot answer

base.update_signal: the delivery contract, the significant-surface convention, or the estimate-versus-claim policy is restated

nodes.definition: Bind every electrical setpoint to its two legitimate authorities: the supplier's technical data sheet for the specific commercial bath (its current-density window, temperature and agitation class, replenishment terms) and the shop's own log of measured runs (its actual minutes-per-micron by bath and geometry, its burn incidents, its meter cross-check history). Published handbook-class ranges — such as the corpus orientation that rack-scale gold baths run tenths-of-an-ampere to low single amperes per square decimeter depending on family — may be cited only as handbook-class orientation, never as a setpoint. The doctrine is what lets this KB teach mechanisms (what a parameter does, how drift shows) while the numbers live where they belong: TDS first, log second, habit never.

excluded: bath chemistry analysis and replenishment decisions
inventing or asserting universal setpoints

pros.claim: TDS-first discipline makes every setpoint defensible and transferable between operators
pros.example: a new bench hand runs the same acid hard gold job to the same window because the setpoint sheet cites the TDS clause, not a predecessor's habit

cons.claim: A TDS window is broad, so it alone cannot tell the shop where inside it this tank runs best
cons.example: two shops on the same commercial product settle at different in-window current densities because their agitation and racking differ

failure_modes: running a remembered setpoint from a previous product on a new bath's first fill
citing a handbook range as if it were the product's own window
acceptance_tests: every setpoint on the run sheet traces to a TDS clause or a logged measured run, and any handbook-class figure is labeled as orientation
revisit_triggers: the supplier issues a TDS revision or the shop switches products
the log accumulates runs that contradict a TDS-derived assumption

base.update_signal: a TDS revision lands or logged runs contradict the current setpoint sheet

nodes.definition: Draw the hard electrical boundary of the bench: all work happens downstream of the rectifier's manufacturer-sanctioned connections — output leads, sanctioned splitters, sanctioned auxiliary outputs — and nothing upstream or inside is ever opened, bypassed or improvised. Heaters, electrolyte and mains power share a wet room, so the obligation classes apply as content: residual-current protection and equipment condition per the maker and the jurisdiction's workplace-electrical rules, dry hands and intact insulation at the tank, no lone improvisation, and a failing unit leaves service for qualified repair. Low-voltage DC at the work is the operating area; a blown meter, a scorched lead or a ripple complaint is a service event, not a soldering-iron evening.

excluded: mains-side or internal rectifier work
chemical safety segregation rules owned by the safety specialist

pros.claim: A bright-line service rule removes the single most tempting bench improvisation under deadline
pros.example: a rectifier with a dead panel meter is tagged out and the batch waits, instead of being run by feel on a Friday afternoon

cons.claim: Strict adherence idles the line when the only rectifier faults mid-week
cons.example: a one-rectifier shop loses two days of plating waiting for manufacturer service rather than jury-rigging a spare supply

failure_modes: improvised auxiliary wiring or mains-side fixes that put current or fault paths where no instruction sanctioned them
running a unit with known meter or lead damage because the schedule is tight
acceptance_tests: no connection on the bench exists that the equipment manufacturer's instructions do not sanction, and every known-faulty unit is tagged out of service
revisit_triggers: new equipment arrives or the manufacturer revises its instructions
the jurisdiction's workplace-electrical requirements change

base.update_signal: manufacturer instructions, the equipment roster, or jurisdiction electrical rules change

nodes.definition: Estimate the true plateable area — every immersed conductive surface that will draw current — because amperes are sized as current density times area, so a thirty-percent area error is a thirty-percent current-density error: the difference between bright and burnt. The method classes: geometric decomposition (a plain band is circumference times width times two faces plus edges; a pendant is a disc plus bail), CAD or scan area when a model exists, gauge-and-length arithmetic for wire and chain, and per-SKU area cards frozen from past measured runs for repeat work. A stated complexity allowance covers texture, filigree and chain-link overlap; mixed racks are summed piece by piece, and any robber or auxiliary hardware that will draw current joins the total. Rigor scales with the job: a flash refresh tolerates an eyeball, a heavy-build customer ring does not.

included: decomposition, CAD, gauge-length and SKU-card method classes
summing mixed loads and sacrificial hardware
excluded: rack layout and part positioning (fixturing KB)
pricing the gold from the area

pros.claim: Per-SKU area cards turn the hardest estimation job into a one-time cost for repeat work
pros.example: a trade account's signet ring measured carefully once, then run for two years from its card with first-article checks

cons.claim: Decomposition systematically under-counts textured and pierced work unless the allowance is honest
cons.example: a filigree brooch whose real surface is far above its silhouette area, burning at the set current computed from the silhouette

failure_modes: sizing current from silhouette area on textured or pierced pieces
forgetting the robber or auxiliary hardware in the total and starving the work
acceptance_tests: the area worksheet names its method, states the complexity allowance, sums every current-drawing surface in the load, and is retained with the run record
revisit_triggers: first-article measurements show a systematic thickness bias for a geometry class
a new SKU enters repeat production and earns a card

base.update_signal: a measured run exposes systematic area bias for a geometry class or a new estimation aid (scanner, CAD library) arrives

nodes.definition: Teach current density as the master variable of the deposit: within the TDS window it sets deposition rate, grain size, brightness and color consistency; the window itself belongs to the specific product. Too high — beyond what mass transport can feed — and the deposit burns: dark brown to black, matte and rough, appearing first at edges, tips and other high-current points, often with stressed or powdery structure; the corpus defect tables read burned edges as current too high for the gold content, agitation and area actually present. Too low and the run drags: build time stretches, some chemistries go dull or drift off color at the bottom of their window, and every extra immersed minute multiplies drag-out, staining and schedule cost. CD also trades against temperature, agitation and metal content — all TDS-governed — so a CD decision is never made alone.

included: slow, dull and drag-out costs at low CD
excluded: the numeric window itself (TDS territory)
bath-side levers like temperature and concentration correction (bath-chemistry KB)

pros.claim: Reading the deposit through CD lets one variable explain most bright-work failures before chemistry is blamed
pros.example: burnt earring posts diagnosed as under-counted area (hence CD too high) and fixed by recomputing area, with the bath left alone

cons.claim: The master-variable habit can hide a genuine chemistry fault behind repeated electrical retuning
cons.example: chasing dullness with CD changes for a week when the real cause was organic contamination the bath log would have flagged

failure_modes: raising current to speed a job past the window and burning the high points
attributing every defect to CD and never routing suspicion back to the bath specialist
acceptance_tests: for any proposed current change the operator can state the expected effect on rate, appearance and burn risk, and which TDS clause bounds the change
revisit_triggers: the product or its TDS window changes
logged burns or dullness contradict the taught mechanism for this bath

base.update_signal: a bath change or a run of logged defects revises what CD is observed to control on this line

nodes.definition: Explain the burn threshold as mass transport, not as a magic number: deposition cannot outrun the arrival of gold complex through the depleted layer at the cathode, and as current approaches that limiting value the deposit goes powdery, then burnt. The ceiling rises with agitation (thinner boundary layer), temperature and gold concentration, and falls as a bath depletes — which is why dilute, diffusion-limited acid hard gold leans so hard on agitation that the corpus calls solution movement mandatory for it. The ceiling is located from the TDS window and the shop's logged burn incidents, never by pushing customer work until it scorches; and raising agitation to buy ceiling respects bath-class safety — no air sparge into a cyanide bath, whose mist is an exposure route.

included: what raises and lowers the ceiling
locating the ceiling from TDS plus log
excluded: agitation hardware and part-motion setup (fixturing KB)
bath concentration corrections (bath-chemistry KB)

pros.claim: Knowing the ceiling scales with agitation and metal content turns a burn from mystery into checklist
pros.example: edge burning after a quiet stirrer pump failure is recognized as a lowered ceiling, not a bath fault

cons.claim: The ceiling is invisible until approached, so cautious shops leave real throughput unused
cons.example: a line running far below its agitated ceiling because one historic burn made the house rule ultra-conservative

failure_modes: discovering the ceiling on customer work instead of on a coupon
buying ceiling with an agitation method the bath class forbids, like sparging a cyanide bath
acceptance_tests: the run sheet's current sits inside the TDS window with a stated margin to the last logged burn condition for this bath and geometry class
revisit_triggers: a burn occurs at a setting previously logged as safe
agitation, temperature or metal-content practice changes on the tank

base.update_signal: a burn incident at a supposedly safe setting or a change in agitation practice relocates the observed ceiling

nodes.definition: Plan the run with Faraday's law as a mechanism: deposited mass is proportional to charge, so over a known area, thickness is proportional to ampere-minutes times cathode efficiency — for monovalent gold at density near 19.3 g/cm3 the arithmetic is direct. The bench form: amperes come from target CD times total area; minutes come from the target microns divided by the bath's microns-per-ampere-minute-per-area at its efficiency. Bath family sets the scale of the answer — the corpus orientation is a few minutes per micron at moderate CD in a near-full-efficiency alkaline cyanide bath and several-fold longer in low-efficiency acid hard gold — but both figures are handbook-class orientation: the number the shop actually uses is its own measured minutes-per-micron. The output is a time plan labeled estimate, scheduled to be corrected by the first article.

included: amperes from CD times area, minutes from ampere-minutes per micron
excluded: asserting a universal minutes-per-micron figure
gold cost accounting beyond the plan

pros.claim: Faraday arithmetic gives a defensible starting time for any new job instead of folklore soak times
pros.example: a first-ever heavy pendant gets a computed plan from area and target microns, then a first-article check, instead of somebody's remembered twenty minutes

cons.claim: The arithmetic is only as good as the efficiency assumption hiding inside it
cons.example: an aged acid hard gold bath running far below its handbook-class efficiency delivers half the planned microns in the planned minutes

failure_modes: shipping the arithmetic as the delivered thickness without measurement
reusing another bath family's minutes-per-micron because the numbers were handy
acceptance_tests: every time plan shows its inputs (area, CD, efficiency source) and carries the estimate label with the scheduled first-article verification
revisit_triggers: measured minutes-per-micron drifts from the planning figure
the bath family or product on the line changes

base.update_signal: measured thickness diverges from the arithmetic beyond tolerance or the efficiency source changes

nodes.definition: Treat cathode efficiency as a property of this bath today, never a constant: family sets the class — alkaline cyanide gold runs near full efficiency while acid hard gold runs well under half and falls further with bath age and rising current density, per the corpus's handbook-class ranges — and age, contamination, temperature, gold content and CD move it run to run. Calibration is by measurement: divide the first-article or coupon thickness actually delivered by the ampere-minutes per area actually applied, and the shop owns a measured microns-per-ampere-minute for that bath in that state. The log of those calibrations is the true efficiency curve of the line; any handbook-derived figure in a plan is flagged unverified until a measurement replaces it, and a sagging curve is routed to the bath specialist as an aging signal.

included: efficiency-trend hand-off to the bath specialist
excluded: bath analysis and correction (bath-chemistry KB)
guaranteeing an efficiency figure to a customer

pros.claim: A measured efficiency curve converts every future plan from guess to interpolation
pros.example: the third month of an acid hard gold bath plans at its own logged curve and lands first articles inside tolerance repeatedly

cons.claim: Calibration burns measurement time and only holds while the bath state holds
cons.example: a curve painstakingly built before a carbon treatment becomes obsolete the day the treatment changes the bath

failure_modes: planning batch two on the efficiency the bath had months ago
silently absorbing an efficiency collapse instead of flagging bath aging to the chemistry side
acceptance_tests: each bath on the line carries a dated measured microns-per-ampere-minute entry, and plans cite either that entry or an explicit unverified flag
revisit_triggers: a new first-article or coupon measurement lands
the bath undergoes treatment, replenishment beyond routine, or replacement

base.update_signal: a fresh calibration measurement or a bath-state change (treatment, heavy replenishment, remake) lands

nodes.definition: Set the rectifier the way thickness control demands: constant-current mode, because thickness is charge-controlled — current is the held variable and cell voltage falls where the chemistry and geometry put it (typically a few volts at rack scale, geometry dependent, per the corpus). Amperes are sized as target current density times the total immersed area, work plus any robber or auxiliary hardware; the current limit is set before entry so a bumped knob cannot exceed the window. Ripple matters for bright work — low-ripple output is the corpus's stated preference for bright deposits — and ripple performance is the manufacturer's specification to meet, not the bench's to modify. Everything here happens within the maker's instructions; sizing, mode and limits are bench decisions, the box itself never is.

included: ampere sizing from CD times total area
pre-set current limits and ripple as a manufacturer spec
excluded: voltage-controlled decorative flash practice not on this line's spec
internal rectifier service or modification

pros.claim: Constant current makes delivered charge — and so thickness — directly bookable from the panel and the clock
pros.example: a run at a held two amperes for a logged time yields ampere-minutes the record can convert to expected microns

cons.claim: Held current on a shrinking effective area concentrates CD wherever contact or immersion is partial
cons.example: solution level dropping mid-run shrinks immersed area and quietly pushes the true CD above plan at the waterline

failure_modes: running voltage-controlled by habit so delivered charge is unknowable
sizing amperes from work area alone while a robber quietly draws its share
acceptance_tests: the run sheet shows mode, the ampere setting derived as CD times total summed area, and a pre-set current limit inside the TDS window
revisit_triggers: equipment change or manufacturer instruction revision
a run where actual immersed area diverged from the plan (level drop, partial contact)

base.update_signal: a new rectifier, a revised manufacturer instruction, or a logged mode/sizing failure changes the setup rule

nodes.definition: Trust no meter unverified: the panel ammeter is cross-checked against a reference — a clamp meter or a calibrated shunt used per its own instructions — on a fixed schedule and after any anomaly, because every micron the shop books rides on that current reading. Cell voltage at held current is the free diagnostic: abnormally high voltage flags failing contacts, a worn insoluble-anode coating or a starved conductive path; abnormally low flags a short or a grossly over-counted area. The verdict rule is absolute: when panel and reference disagree beyond the shop's tolerance, the reference wins, the unit is tagged for manufacturer service, and runs logged since the last good cross-check are flagged for thickness re-verification — nobody compensates a drifting meter by feel.

included: cell voltage as contact and anode diagnostic
excluded: repairing or recalibrating the rectifier internally
contact-point placement on the piece (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: A cheap clamp-meter habit protects every thickness number the shop will ever log
pros.example: a panel ammeter found reading ten percent high explains a month of slightly thin first articles before a customer does

cons.claim: Cross-checking adds a ritual that feels redundant exactly as long as it finds nothing
cons.example: months of green cross-checks tempt a busy bench to stretch the schedule until the drift arrives unobserved

failure_modes: booking ampere-minutes from a drifted panel meter for weeks
reading high cell voltage and pressing on instead of stopping to find the failing contact or anode
acceptance_tests: a dated cross-check record exists for every rectifier in service, and any disagreement beyond tolerance shows a service tag plus flagged back-runs
revisit_triggers: a cross-check fails or the tolerance policy changes
an unexplained thickness bias appears across jobs on one rectifier

base.update_signal: a failed cross-check, a new reference instrument, or a change in the verification schedule

nodes.definition: Enforce live entry as an unconditional habit: current flows before the work touches solution, at strike and at build, every time. The mechanism it defeats is immersion (displacement) deposition — gold plating itself chemically onto a less-noble surface with no current — which produces the smutty, non-adherent film the corpus names as the root of strike-less adhesion failure; everything plated over that film peels later, usually in the customer's hands. Dead entry is not recoverable by more plating: a load that went in dead comes out, and the piece routes to the strip-and-replate decision (quality specialist's gate) with the event logged. The discipline is electrical timing — switch on, verify current at the expected level, then immerse — and it costs seconds against the hours a peeling batch costs.

excluded: strike bath selection and chemistry (layer-architecture and bath KBs)
the strip/replate execution itself (quality specialist)

pros.claim: One timing habit eliminates a whole class of adhesion failures that surface weeks after delivery
pros.example: a bench that verifies amperes on the meter before every immersion never meets the peeling-bracelet return that a dead entry seeded

cons.claim: Live entry disciplines the whole entry choreography, which slows dense multi-rack sessions
cons.example: each of a dozen racks entering a small tank needs its own switch-verify-immerse cycle instead of a batched dunk

failure_modes: immersing while reaching for the switch because the sequence felt obvious
plating over a suspected dead entry to save the schedule
acceptance_tests: the entry procedure requires current verified at the expected level before immersion, and any dead-entry event shows a stop, a routing decision and a log line
revisit_triggers: an adhesion failure traces back to entry practice
tank or switching hardware changes the entry choreography

base.update_signal: an adhesion failure attributed to entry, or a hardware change that alters the switch-verify-immerse sequence

nodes.definition: Read the piece before the run: current crowds onto edges, tips, points, outer rims and anything nearest the anode — the high-CD zones where burning and over-build start — and starves recesses, bores, ring interiors and deep relief — the low-CD zones that come out thin and off-color. The spread is set by geometry, anode placement and the bath's throwing power, a bath-class property that differs between families. The output is a zone map, even a sixty-second sketch: where this piece will burn first, where it will starve, and where the spec's significant surfaces sit inside that field. The map is what decides whether the run needs a shield, a robber or an auxiliary anode, and it dictates where verification must measure — because an easy flat reading proves nothing about a starved bore.

included: zone prediction from geometry and anode line-of-sight
throwing power as a bath-class property
excluded: computing field solutions numerically
rack positioning mechanics (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: A one-minute zone sketch prevents the two classic surprises: burnt tips and hollow-back thinness
pros.example: a leaf brooch mapped before the run gets its serrated edge shielded and its concave back flagged for coupon verification

cons.claim: Intuition-based maps mislead on geometries the bench has not met before
cons.example: a mesh bracelet whose interior links starve far worse than the sketch predicted because mesh shadows itself

failure_modes: running a deep-relief piece with no map and discovering the starved zone at QC
measuring only convenient flats so the map is never tested against reality
acceptance_tests: every complex-geometry run shows a zone map naming its high and low CD areas and where the significant surfaces fall within them
revisit_triggers: measured thickness spread contradicts the predicted map for a geometry class
anode configuration or bath family (throwing power class) changes

base.update_signal: a measured spread that contradicts the map, or a change of anode configuration or bath throwing-power class

nodes.definition: Run the anode side as an electrical-delivery lever: insoluble anodes of the platinized-titanium or MMO-coated-titanium classes, sized at an anode-to-cathode area ratio of at least one-to-one and ideally larger per the corpus, placed symmetric to the work at even spacing — greater distance smooths distribution, close anodes exaggerate the high-CD zones facing them. Material discipline is bath-governed: never bare stainless in acid gold chemistry, where it dissolves iron, chromium and nickel into the bath. Anode condition is read electrically and visually: a worn precious-metal-oxide coating shows as creeping cell voltage at held current and as roughness or nodules seeded by shed fragments; a worn anode is replaced or recoated per its maker, and the chemical consequences of anode faults route to the bath specialist.

included: insoluble anode classes and never-stainless-in-acid-gold rule
area ratio, symmetry and spacing as distribution levers
excluded: gold replenishment chemistry (gold comes from salt, not the anode — bath KB)
anode contamination remediation (bath-chemistry KB)

pros.claim: Symmetric, generously sized anodes flatten distribution before any corrective hardware is needed
pros.example: moving from one side anode to a facing pair visibly evens the color on both faces of a plated locket

cons.claim: Anode work is easy to overlook because its failures masquerade as bath or rectifier trouble
cons.example: weeks of creeping cell voltage blamed on the rectifier until the anode's worn coating is finally inspected

failure_modes: an undersized or lopsided anode starving one face of every load
running a stainless anode in acid gold and contaminating the bath with iron and nickel
acceptance_tests: the tank sheet records anode class, area ratio and placement, and a periodic condition check covering coating wear and voltage trend
revisit_triggers: cell-voltage trend or deposit roughness implicates anode wear
tank reconfiguration changes anode count or placement

base.update_signal: anode wear findings, a reconfiguration of the tank, or a bath-class change that alters anode material rules

nodes.definition: Tame high-CD zones with two classes of hardware, chosen in cost order. A shield — a non-conductive baffle interposed between anode and the hot zone — reduces local current density and consumes nothing; it is the first answer for burning edges and rims wherever geometry gives it a place to sit. A current robber (thief) — a sacrificial cathodic surface wired near the hot zone — draws off the excess current when no shield can reach, and it plates gold onto itself: a real gold cost and an arithmetic obligation, because the robber's area joins the total for ampere sizing and its stolen share breaks piece-only Faraday time math. Recurring geometry earns a shop template (a shaped shield or robber kept with the SKU card) so the fix is repeatable, not re-improvised per run.

included: shields-before-robbers cost order and template reuse
excluded: auxiliary anodes for starved zones (their own node)
robber gold-reclaim accounting (business and bath territory)

pros.claim: A shaped shield solves an edge-burn class permanently at zero consumable cost
pros.example: a slotted acrylic baffle kept with the chain-clasp SKU card ends the recurring scorched-clasp-tip defect

cons.claim: A robber quietly spends gold and skews the time plan when its draw goes uncounted
cons.example: a batch comes out ten percent thin because the robber's area never entered the ampere sizing

failure_modes: reaching for a robber where a shield would do, paying gold for geometry
leaving the robber out of the area sum and under-plating the work
acceptance_tests: any run using a shield or robber names it on the run sheet, and a robber's area appears in the ampere-sizing sum with its gold noted as job cost
revisit_triggers: a template shield or robber stops matching its geometry class
first articles on robber runs show a systematic thickness bias

base.update_signal: a template proves wrong for its geometry class or robber-run measurements expose a sizing bias

nodes.definition: Feed low-CD zones with the auxiliary-anode class: a small insoluble anode — platinized-titanium or MMO, same material discipline as the main anode — placed into or near the starved feature (inside a bangle, down the bowl of a deep pendant, along a bore) so the field reaches what the main anode cannot see. Wiring is the boundary: an auxiliary runs only on a method the equipment maker sanctions — a separate controlled output or a maker-sanctioned balancing arrangement — never a bench-improvised resistor lash-up. Its risks are concentration in miniature: it can short against the work (a burn spot at the touch point) and it can over-plate its local zone, so auxiliary runs carry mechanical standoffs, closer in-run watching and coupon or XRF verification of the zone it was meant to save; where no sanctioned wiring exists, the honest alternatives are repositioning, accepting and disclosing the spread, or declining the geometry.

excluded: improvised electrical arrangements of any kind
brush/selective plating as a different delivery mode (fixturing KB names it)

pros.claim: A correctly wired auxiliary is the only way some interior geometries ever reach a specified minimum
pros.example: a wide bangle's interior meets its micron spec only after a rod auxiliary is run down its axis on the rectifier's second output

cons.claim: An auxiliary adds a live electrode in close quarters with the work and all the failure modes that implies
cons.example: a pendant swinging on its rack touches the auxiliary and takes a burn spot that costs a strip-and-replate

failure_modes: improvised auxiliary wiring outside the maker's instructions
an auxiliary shorting to the work or silently over-plating its local zone unverified
acceptance_tests: every auxiliary run names the sanctioned wiring method, shows a mechanical standoff, and verifies the target zone by coupon or XRF
revisit_triggers: an auxiliary incident (short, local over-plate) occurs
the equipment maker adds or withdraws a sanctioned wiring option

base.update_signal: an auxiliary incident or a change in the maker's sanctioned wiring options

nodes.definition: Watch the run instead of trusting it: at held current the cell voltage is the run's vital sign — steady is health, a steady climb flags a corroding contact or a wearing anode coating, a sudden drop flags a short (work against anode or auxiliary); the gas pattern and solution movement confirm the agitation the ceiling depends on; and the deposit's developing appearance at the mapped high-CD points is the early-warning display, because the first darkening at an edge arrives minutes before a scrapped load. The stop rule is explicit: visible burn onset, a voltage excursion beyond the run sheet's band, or any suspected short stops the run now — a planned interruption per procedure costs a logged line in the ampere-minute bookkeeping, a pressed-on burn costs the batch. Chemical judgment of what is seen (color drift, haze diagnosis) routes to the bath and quality specialists.

included: appearance watch at mapped hot points
explicit stop rule and logged interruptions
excluded: chemical diagnosis of observed defects (bath and quality specialists)
unattended-run automation design

pros.claim: Watching the mapped hot points converts burn from a batch loss into a seconds-long correction
pros.example: the first matte tinge on a pendant's tip triggers a stop and current recheck, and the piece polishes out instead of stripping

cons.claim: Full attention per run caps how many tanks one operator can honestly supervise
cons.example: three simultaneous racks in three tanks leave no one actually watching the acid gold tank's edges

failure_modes: walking away from a run whose voltage band was never written down
noting an excursion and finishing the run anyway to keep the schedule
acceptance_tests: each run sheet carries a voltage band and named watch points, and every interruption or excursion appears as a logged line with its response
revisit_triggers: a stop criterion fires wrongly or demonstrably too late
tank count per operator or supervision practice changes

base.update_signal: a stop-rule failure in either direction, or a change in how many runs one operator supervises

nodes.definition: Measure the first article of every batch before committing the rest: XRF thickness readings at the significant surfaces — including the high-wear points and the suspected low-CD zones from the map, not just the easy flat — compared against the Faraday plan. The corpus's own warning motivates the ritual: efficiency drifts with bath age, so the rate assumption is re-verified by XRF on the first article every batch. Inside tolerance, the batch runs on the confirmed plan; outside, the run plan is recalibrated (and the efficiency log updated) before piece two enters the tank. XRF access may be an owned bench unit or a service arrangement — the discipline is identical, only the turnaround changes — and the reading is recorded against the job, because this measurement is what the delivery claim will stand on. Formal acceptance protocols beyond thickness (adhesion, porosity) belong to the quality specialist.

included: measuring at significant and suspect zones
excluded: full QC acceptance testing and claims (quality specialist)
XRF instrument physics and calibration internals

pros.claim: One measured article converts the whole batch from arithmetic risk to verified plan
pros.example: a fifty-piece run proceeds confidently after piece one reads on target at the wear band and the mapped recess

cons.claim: Service-lab XRF turnaround stalls batches for shops without an owned unit
cons.example: a same-day trade promise breaks because the first article spends a day at the testing service

failure_modes: running the whole batch on the plan and measuring afterward, discovering the shortfall fifty pieces deep
measuring only a flat back that neither wears nor starves and calling the piece verified
acceptance_tests: each batch shows a first-article measurement at named significant and suspect zones, a compare-to-plan verdict, and any recalibration applied before the batch continued
revisit_triggers: the tolerance policy or XRF access arrangement changes
repeated first-article misses implicate the plan inputs upstream

base.update_signal: a change in tolerance policy, XRF access, or a pattern of first-article misses pointing upstream

nodes.definition: Run a witness coupon — a small piece of known substrate and measured area — with the load when the geometry defeats direct measurement: bores, deep relief, interior surfaces where an XRF beam cannot land. Position is the method's heart: a coupon wired at the worst-case low-CD position proves the minimum; a coupon at a standardized position gives run-to-run comparability; a coupon hung where it was convenient proves only itself, and its number is labeled non-representative. The coupon's measured thickness divided into the applied ampere-minutes also feeds the efficiency calibration, making every coupon double duty: delivery evidence and bath telemetry. Its limits are stated honestly — a coupon approximates, it does not become, the recess it stands for — so coupon-verified minimums carry their positioning note into the record.

included: coupon-fed efficiency calibration and labeling of limits
excluded: destructive cross-section metallography
acceptance decisions built on the coupon (quality specialist consumes the evidence)

pros.claim: A worst-case coupon is the only honest minimum-thickness evidence for geometry XRF cannot reach
pros.example: a coupon wired inside a napkin-ring's bore substantiates the interior micron statement no beam could make

cons.claim: A coupon at the wrong position manufactures false confidence in the exact zone that needed proof
cons.example: a coupon hung outside the bangle reads on target while the true interior runs thin

failure_modes: placing the coupon for convenience and reporting it as the recess
reusing a coupon of unknown area so the efficiency arithmetic is polluted
acceptance_tests: every coupon record names its substrate, measured area and position class (worst-case, standard, or non-representative), and its reading feeds the efficiency log
revisit_triggers: a coupon reading diverges from an on-piece XRF at the same nominal zone
a new geometry class needs its worst-case position defined

base.update_signal: coupon-versus-XRF divergence at a matched zone or a new geometry class requiring a defined worst-case position

nodes.definition: Judge delivery where it matters: the spec names the significant surfaces — wear bands, visible faces, skin-contact areas — and delivering the microns means the minimum thickness there, not a flattering average across the piece. Low-CD zones inside the significant set are measured, never assumed from a flat's reading; the spread between best and worst zones is recorded and, when a starved zone falls short, the shortfall is disclosed and decided, not shipped silently. One compliance flag is hard-wired: a starved zone that leaves thin gold over a nickel underplate on skin-contact jewelry raises the nickel-release compliance class (a regulated limit class in several jurisdictions — verify the rules where the piece sells) and routes the piece to the layer-architecture and compliance decision rather than out the door. Formal acceptance testing and the customer-facing claim itself belong to the quality specialist; this node hands over the measured verdict they act on.

included: nickel-release compliance flag for starved skin-contact zones
excluded: setting the significant-surface list (intake/spec)
approving label claims like vermeil (quality and compliance specialists)

pros.claim: Judging minimum-at-significant-surface is what makes a micron statement mean something on a real shaped piece
pros.example: a ring passes only when its wear band — not its sheltered inner shank — carries the specified microns

cons.claim: Minimum-based judgment fails pieces whose average delivery looks generous, which costs rework and hard conversations
cons.example: a pendant averaging well above spec is held because its mapped recess within the visible face reads thin

failure_modes: certifying delivery from an average or from a non-significant flat
shipping a starved skin-contact zone over nickel without raising the compliance class
acceptance_tests: the delivery verdict lists each significant surface with its measured minimum, records the spread, and shows the nickel-release flag decision for any starved skin-contact zone over a nickel underplate
revisit_triggers: the spec's significant-surface definition changes
a compliance rule touching nickel release or marking classes changes in a selling jurisdiction

base.update_signal: the significant-surface convention or a jurisdiction compliance rule (nickel release, marking classes) changes

nodes.definition: Close every run with its electrical record: estimated area and the method that produced it, set current and the CD it implies, run time with every interruption, total ampere-minutes, planned versus measured thickness, and any shield, robber or auxiliary hardware used. This page is what turns Faraday from handbook arithmetic into shop knowledge — it feeds the measured minutes-per-micron curve, matures SKU cards, hands the ampere-minute figure to the bath side's gold-replenishment bookkeeping (the replenishment decision itself is the bath specialist's), and answers the only question that matters when a job is challenged months later: what exactly was done. It is deliberately the electrical page of the job log, not the whole log — tank sequence, rinses and handling live in the fixturing KB's run logging.

included: feeds to efficiency curve, SKU cards and replenishment bookkeeping
excluded: the full multi-tank job log (fixturing KB)
replenishment decisions and bath analysis records (bath-chemistry KB)

pros.claim: Planned-versus-measured on every run makes drift visible before it becomes a customer problem
pros.example: three consecutive runs each a little under plan reveal the efficiency sag a single run would have hidden

cons.claim: Record discipline feels like overhead on small jobs and erodes exactly when the bench is busiest
cons.example: a rush week of unrecorded flash jobs leaves the minutes-per-micron curve blind for the month

failure_modes: recording plan numbers but never the measured outcome, so the record cannot teach
omitting interruptions so the booked ampere-minutes overstate delivered charge
acceptance_tests: every run record contains area with method, current, time with interruptions, ampere-minutes, planned and measured thickness, and hardware used — with no field blank
revisit_triggers: the record template changes or a consumer (efficiency curve, SKU cards, replenishment bookkeeping) changes its needs
a challenged job exposes a missing field

base.update_signal: a template change, a new record consumer, or a challenged job exposing a gap in the fields

edges.why_related: the setpoint doctrine exists to serve the delivery contract the frame states
the electrical boundary scopes what the bench may touch while executing the delivery contract
area estimation is the first quantity the delivery contract demands before current can be sized
the CD mechanism is taught inside the doctrine that keeps its numbers in the TDS and the log
the ceiling is the upper boundary of the master variable the mechanism node defines
Faraday arithmetic converts thickness to time only over a known plateable area
the chosen in-window CD is the current input of the time plan
calibration corrects the efficiency factor inside the Faraday plan with measured runs
the shop log the doctrine mandates is where measured minutes-per-micron lives
ampere sizing is CD times the summed area the estimation node produces
the rectifier setting realizes the target CD the mechanism node bounds
meter verification certifies the instrument the setup node relies on for its held current
live entry presumes a rectifier already set and limited so current can flow before immersion
the zone map applies the CD mechanism spatially across a real geometry
anode area, symmetry and spacing are the first levers the map's predictions call for
shields and robbers are deployed against the high-CD zones the map identifies
auxiliary anodes are deployed into the starved zones the map identifies
in-run voltage and current watching is only meaningful on verified meters
the burn-watch half of monitoring exists because the run operates below a ceiling that can move
the first-article measurement exists to test the Faraday plan before the batch commits
the coupon closes the same estimate-to-measurement loop where XRF geometry fails
the map defines the worst-case position that gives a coupon its evidentiary value
the delivery verdict is built from the first-article readings at the significant surfaces
coupon evidence substantiates minimums at surfaces the beam cannot reach
the map tells the delivery judgment which significant surfaces sit in starved zones and must be measured
the record books the plan's inputs and its ampere-minutes as the run's planned side
the measured outcome completes the record's planned-versus-measured pair
setup choices are confined to modes, limits and connections the manufacturer's instructions sanction
auxiliary wiring may use only maker-sanctioned methods, never bench improvisation
the watch begins the moment a live entry starts the deposit
a run watched to clean completion hands its first article to measurement
each measured first article updates the bath's measured microns-per-ampere-minute
accumulated run records become the shop-log half of the setpoint authority
an area error propagates one-for-one into a CD error at the held current, which is how mis-measured pieces burn
a wearing anode coating drives the creeping cell voltage the in-run watch is trained to catch
a robber steals current and gold, so piece-only ampere-minute arithmetic overstates what the work received
edges.resolution_rule: whenever a robber is wired, its area enters the ampere sizing and the batch time is set by the first-article measurement, never by raw piece-only Faraday arithmetic

edges.why_related: schedule pressure pushes the current setting up toward the ceiling that the deposit cannot survive crossing
edges.resolution_rule: the TDS window and the logged ceiling win unconditionally: current is never raised past them to shorten a run — throughput is bought with load size and scheduling, not current density

edges.why_related: the urge to feed a starved zone tempts improvised wiring the manufacturer never sanctioned
edges.resolution_rule: the manufacturer-instruction boundary wins: an auxiliary runs only on a sanctioned wiring method; otherwise the options are repositioning, disclosed acceptance of the spread, or declining the geometry

edges.why_related: both are measurement classes closing the Faraday loop, chosen by whether the geometry admits a direct beam or needs a proxy

conflict_axes.name: throughput_speed_vs_burn_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: Raising current density shortens run time until it crosses the mass-transport ceiling and scraps the load; deadline pressure always points up, deposit quality always points down.
poles: raise CD to cut run time
hold CD safely inside window and ceiling
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the TDS window and logged ceiling are hard bounds; buy throughput with bigger verified loads and scheduling, never with current

conflict_axes.name: estimate_trust_vs_measurement_cost
conflict_axes.description: Faraday arithmetic is nearly free while XRF and coupons cost money and turnaround, tempting the bench to ship on arithmetic.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the estimate plans, the measurement certifies: first article measured every batch, and no delivery statement rests on arithmetic alone

conflict_axes.name: area_precision_vs_bench_time
conflict_axes.description: Careful area decomposition of every piece is slow, while eyeball estimates are fast and wrong exactly on the textured pieces that matter most.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: scale rigor with thickness spec and job risk, and amortize the careful work into per-SKU area cards for repeat pieces

conflict_axes.name: uniformity_engineering_vs_gold_cost
conflict_axes.description: Robbers and auxiliary anodes flatten the thickness spread but consume gold, hardware and setup time on every run they join.
poles: accept the spread and spend nothing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: engineer only where the spec demands a minimum in a low zone; where it does not, accept the spread and record it honestly

conflict_axes.name: handbook_orientation_vs_tds_authority
conflict_axes.description: Published handbook-class ranges are broadly right and always available, while the product's TDS is specific and binding — and they sometimes disagree.
poles: run only on the product TDS and shop log
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: handbook ranges orient understanding and never set a knob; the TDS governs and the shop's measured log refines within it

conflict_axes.name: equipment_boundary_vs_deadline
conflict_axes.description: A faulty rectifier or a missing sanctioned output invites improvisation exactly when the schedule is tightest.
poles: improvise to keep the line moving
stay inside manufacturer instructions and wait
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: safety and the manufacturer boundary beat throughput, cost and deadline everywhere they meet; a faulty unit leaves service

conflict_axes.name: average_delivery_vs_worst_zone_minimum
conflict_axes.description: A piece can average above spec while its starved significant zone runs thin; averages flatter the bench and betray the wearer.
poles: certify on minimum at significant surfaces
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the significant-surface definition wins: measure the mapped worst zones within it and disclose any shortfall instead of averaging it away

conflict_axes.name: record_discipline_vs_run_pace
conflict_axes.description: Complete electrical records slow a busy bench, and skipping fields is invisible until the curve goes blind or a job is challenged.
poles: keep the line moving and log later
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the minimum field set that feeds verification and the shop history is never skipped; planned-versus-measured is the one pair that must survive any rush

conflict_axes.name: coupon_fidelity_vs_convenience
conflict_axes.description: A coupon wired where it is easy to hang reads beautifully and proves nothing about the recess it was supposed to represent.
poles: place the coupon at the true worst case
place the coupon where it is convenient
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: position is part of the method: worst-case placement or the reading is labeled non-representative and cannot back a minimum

edge_cases.description: Dark matte edges appear on a filigree pendant minutes into the run
edge_cases.trigger: high-CD points cross the limiting current because the silhouette-based area estimate under-counted the pierced surface
edge_cases.mitigation: stop on first darkening, recompute area with an honest complexity allowance, reset current inside the window, and route bath suspicion to the chemistry side before re-entry

edge_cases.description: A ring's interior reads near-zero thickness while its outside meets spec
edge_cases.trigger: the bore is a low-CD zone the main anode cannot see and longer time only thickens the outside more
edge_cases.mitigation: use a maker-sanctioned auxiliary anode for the bore or disclose the spread against the significant-surface definition; never answer a distribution problem with more minutes

edge_cases.description: The first-article XRF reads far below the Faraday plan on an aged acid hard gold bath
edge_cases.trigger: planning on a handbook-class efficiency while the bath's real efficiency has sagged with age
edge_cases.mitigation: recalibrate minutes-per-micron from the measurement, complete the piece under the corrected plan, log the new efficiency point, and flag the sag to the bath specialist

edge_cases.description: The panel ammeter and the clamp meter disagree well beyond tolerance
edge_cases.trigger: meter drift or a failing shunt inside the rectifier
edge_cases.mitigation: the reference wins: tag the unit for manufacturer service, flag runs since the last good cross-check for thickness re-verification, and never compensate a drifting meter by feel

edge_cases.description: Cell voltage climbs steadily mid-run at held current
edge_cases.trigger: a corroding contact or a worn insoluble-anode coating raising the circuit's resistance
edge_cases.mitigation: make a planned interruption per procedure, inspect contact and anode coating, log the interruption so booked ampere-minutes stay true, and resume only on a healthy circuit

edge_cases.description: A rack of pieces went into the gold tank before the current was switched on
edge_cases.trigger: entry choreography broke down during a busy multi-rack session
edge_cases.mitigation: withdraw the load, treat the immersion film as an adhesion failure in the making, route to the strip/replate decision with the event logged — plating over it is not a repair

edge_cases.description: A mixed rack carries a large flat pendant next to fine chain pieces
edge_cases.trigger: one current setting cannot hold both geometries inside the CD window simultaneously
edge_cases.mitigation: split the load by area class or size current to the summed area with the most burn-prone piece watched as the limiting case and verified first; rack layout mechanics belong to the fixturing discipline

edge_cases.description: Pieces on a robber-equipped run come out systematically under target
edge_cases.trigger: the robber's area never entered the ampere sizing so the work ran below its intended CD
edge_cases.mitigation: re-size amperes with the robber's area included, set batch time from a measured first article, and book the robber's gold as job cost rather than ignoring it

edge_cases.description: A starved recess on a skin-contact bracelet leaves thin gold over its nickel underplate
edge_cases.trigger: the low-CD zone within a significant skin-contact surface under-delivered
edge_cases.mitigation: raise the nickel-release compliance class (verify the selling jurisdiction's rules), hold the piece, and route to the layer-architecture and compliance decision instead of shipping

edge_cases.description: A customer wants a guaranteed micron figure on a deep-relief piece without paying for measurement
edge_cases.trigger: a thickness claim is requested that no measurement will back
edge_cases.mitigation: state the estimate as an estimate naming its method, decline the unmeasured guarantee, and escalate the claim-versus-price decision to intake and the quality specialist

edge_cases.description: Bright work comes out faintly streaky and dull on one aging rectifier only
edge_cases.trigger: output ripple has degraded beyond what bright deposits tolerate
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm by swapping the job to a healthy unit, send the aging rectifier to manufacturer service, and never add improvised filtering at the bench

edge_cases.description: An auxiliary anode drifts and touches the workpiece mid-run
edge_cases.trigger: a missing or failed mechanical standoff lets the swinging piece reach the live auxiliary
edge_cases.mitigation: stop immediately on the voltage drop, assess the burn spot for rework routing, and refit the standoff per the equipment class before any repeat run

workflow.description: Read target microns, named significant surfaces, bath system and stack off the job spec and state the measurement that will certify delivery
workflow.gate: target thickness, significant surfaces, bath/stack and certification method are all stated before any planning begins

workflow.action: Pull the TDS window and shop history
workflow.description: Assemble the setpoint sheet from the product TDS and the logged measured runs for this bath and geometry class
workflow.gate: no setpoint on the sheet lacks a TDS clause or shop-log citation; handbook figures are labeled orientation

workflow.description: Check rectifier, leads and connections against the maker's instructions and tag out anything faulty
workflow.gate: no unsanctioned connection exists on the bench and no known-faulty unit is in service

workflow.description: Compute total immersed conductive area by a named method with a complexity allowance, summing every piece and any sacrificial hardware
workflow.gate: the worksheet names its method, states the allowance, and sums the full current-drawing load

workflow.action: Set current from the CD window
workflow.description: Derive amperes as target CD times total area, set constant-current mode and pre-set the current limit
workflow.gate: the setpoint sits inside the TDS window with stated margin to the logged burn ceiling, and the limit is set before entry

workflow.description: Convert target microns to minutes via ampere-minutes per area at the bath's efficiency figure
workflow.gate: the plan shows its area, CD and efficiency inputs, and the efficiency source is a measured log entry or carries an unverified flag

workflow.action: Map distribution and place corrective hardware
workflow.description: Sketch high and low CD zones, position anodes, and deploy shields, robbers or maker-sanctioned auxiliaries where the spec demands
workflow.gate: high and low zones are named against the significant surfaces, and any robber or auxiliary area is added to the sizing sum

workflow.description: Cross-check the panel meter if due, confirm polarity and expected current, then immerse with current already flowing
workflow.gate: reference agreement is current, and amperes are verified flowing before the work touches solution

workflow.description: Hold the voltage band, watch gas pattern and the mapped hot points, stop on burn onset, excursion or suspected short
workflow.gate: no unexplained excursion stands, and every interruption is logged into the ampere-minute bookkeeping

workflow.description: XRF the first article (or read the witness coupon) at significant and suspect zones and compare to plan
workflow.gate: measured thickness at named zones sits inside tolerance of plan, or the plan is recalibrated before the batch continues

workflow.action: Judge delivery at the significant surfaces
workflow.description: Compare measured minimums at each significant surface against spec, record the spread, and apply the nickel-release flag where a starved skin-contact zone sits over nickel
workflow.gate: every significant surface has a measured minimum, shortfalls are disclosed not averaged away, and any compliance flag is routed

workflow.description: Book area, current, time, interruptions, ampere-minutes and planned-versus-measured, feeding the efficiency curve and SKU cards
workflow.gate: no field is blank and the planned-versus-measured pair is present, with hardware used noted

dominance_rules.rule: The product TDS and the shop's measured log beat any handbook range or remembered habit
dominance_rules.rationale: setpoints asserted from memory or generic tables are the root of invented-figure failures this program forbids
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed setpoint conflicts with the TDS window or with logged measured runs
dominance_rules.action: run the TDS/log value and record why the other figure was rejected

dominance_rules.rule: The manufacturer-instruction boundary beats every deadline
dominance_rules.rationale: improvised electrical work in a wet room risks people and premises, which no schedule justifies
dominance_rules.trigger: an equipment fault or missing sanctioned option tempts a bench workaround
dominance_rules.action: tag the unit or decline the arrangement, reschedule, and use only sanctioned methods

dominance_rules.rule: The burn ceiling beats throughput pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: current above the mass-transport ceiling scraps the load faster than it saves minutes
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal to raise current above the window or logged ceiling to shorten a run
dominance_rules.action: hold current inside the window; recover schedule with load size and sequencing

dominance_rules.rule: A measurement beats an estimate everywhere they disagree
dominance_rules.rationale: Faraday arithmetic carries an efficiency assumption that only measurement can test
dominance_rules.trigger: a Faraday plan and an XRF or coupon reading conflict
dominance_rules.action: believe the measurement, recalibrate the plan, and never release on the arithmetic

dominance_rules.rule: Minimum at significant surfaces beats average thickness in the delivery verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: the wearer meets the worst zone of the wear surface, not the piece's average
dominance_rules.trigger: a piece averages above spec while a significant zone reads below
dominance_rules.action: hold the piece, disclose the shortfall, and decide rework or disclosure with the quality gate

dominance_rules.rule: Live-entry discipline beats the schedule on every load
dominance_rules.rationale: a dead entry seeds an immersion film that fails as peeling in the customer's hands
dominance_rules.trigger: a load entered the tank without current, or entry verification would slow a rush
dominance_rules.action: stop, withdraw any dead-entry load, and route it to strip/replate rather than plating over

dominance_rules.rule: The verified reference meter beats the panel meter
dominance_rules.rationale: every booked ampere-minute rides on the current reading being true
dominance_rules.trigger: panel and reference disagree beyond tolerance
dominance_rules.action: trust the reference, tag the unit for service, and flag back-runs for re-verification

dominance_rules.rule: The nickel-release compliance flag beats shipping pressure on skin-contact goods
dominance_rules.rationale: a starved zone over nickel is a regulated-exposure question, not a cosmetic one
dominance_rules.trigger: thin gold over a nickel underplate is found within a skin-contact significant surface
dominance_rules.action: hold the piece, verify the selling jurisdiction's rules, and route to the compliance decision

dominance_rules.rule: Include-the-hardware arithmetic beats piece-only arithmetic whenever a robber or auxiliary is wired
dominance_rules.rationale: sacrificial and auxiliary surfaces draw real current that piece-only sums ignore
dominance_rules.trigger: a run plan includes any current-drawing hardware beyond the work
dominance_rules.action: sum every current-drawing surface into the sizing and set batch time from the measured first article

anti_rework_rules.rule: Estimate area — with its complexity allowance — before any current is set
anti_rework_rules.prevents: burning textured work at a current sized from silhouette area and paying for a strip-and-replate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pull the TDS window and shop log before writing the run plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: replating a batch run on a remembered setpoint from a different product

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cross-check the panel meter on schedule, before the first job of the day when due
anti_rework_rules.prevents: weeks of thin or thick work booked on a drifted ammeter and re-verified wholesale

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map distribution and place shields, robbers and auxiliaries before the load enters
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mid-run refixturing and starved recesses discovered only at the QC gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify current flowing before every immersion, every load
anti_rework_rules.prevents: adhesion failures from immersion films that surface as peeling weeks after delivery

anti_rework_rules.rule: Measure the first article before committing the batch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an entire batch plated to the wrong thickness on an unverified efficiency assumption

anti_rework_rules.rule: Add robber and auxiliary areas into the ampere sizing at plan time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: under-target work whose current quietly fed the sacrificial hardware

anti_rework_rules.rule: Book planned-versus-measured on every run before the rack leaves the bench
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repeating a drifted efficiency assumption for a month because no record could reveal the trend

iteration_protocol.trigger: a first-article or coupon measurement deviates from the plan beyond tolerance
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the bath's minutes-per-micron from the measurement, correct the running batch, and update the efficiency log

iteration_protocol.trigger: burning or starvation recurs on a geometry class
iteration_protocol.action: revise the zone map for that class and update its template shields, robbers or auxiliary placements

iteration_protocol.trigger: a TDS revision lands or the line switches to a new bath product
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the setpoint sheet from the new TDS, mark all prior efficiency entries stale, and re-verify with a first article
send the unit to manufacturer service and flag every run since the last good cross-check for thickness re-verification

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repeat SKU accumulates enough measured runs to be stable
iteration_protocol.action: freeze its area, current and time into a SKU card and run future jobs from the card with first-article checks

iteration_protocol.trigger: cell voltage trends upward across successive runs on one tank
iteration_protocol.action: inspect contacts and the insoluble-anode coating before the next batch and replace or recoat per the anode maker

iteration_protocol.trigger: a starved skin-contact zone over a nickel underplate is found at delivery judgment
iteration_protocol.action: hold shipment, raise the nickel-release compliance class with a jurisdiction check, and route to the layer-architecture and compliance decision

priority_rationale: The frame nodes (delivery contract, TDS-and-log doctrine, equipment boundary) come first because every later decision presumes a stated target, a legitimate setpoint authority and a hard electrical boundary; area estimation and the current-density mechanism must precede Faraday planning and rectifier sizing, which both consume them; distribution mapping precedes the hardware classes that act on its zones; entry, monitoring and measurement then execute and test the plan; and the delivery verdict and ampere-minute record close the loop last because they judge and archive everything upstream, feeding the shop history that sharpens the next run.
